reviewer: coordinator; exposed to author proposal; not a third independent annotator
method: qualitative source-backed comparison; no aggregate agreement metric

items.finding: Both preserve Marina's attributed nighttime closure report, unspecified agents and lack of corroboration. A separates the unnamed-agent commitment; B includes it in C01. This is not a disagreement.
items.disposition: Compatible candidate commitments; do not duplicate the reporting event merely because an annotation has more rows.

items.finding: Both retain cups/table, still-warm opposite chair and silence. Both classify recent occupancy/company as inferred and not required; opposite whom remains unspecified.
items.disposition: Preserve observations and their inferential availability; do not make a visitor an asserted fact or automatically REQUIRED conclusion.

items.finding: Both distinguish leaver from owner and preserve wetness/non-discovery. Both independently leave the type of stop unspecified; the source does not say bus.
items.disposition: Flag bus-stop narrowing in the author's proposal and legacy candidate as an erratum. Keep frozen artifacts; use generic stop unless a task explicitly licenses narrowing.

items.finding: Both preserve exactly one quoted word and permit English no under the supplied policy. Neither requires a particular refusal context.
items.disposition: Retain lexical mention/count and record translation permission as task policy, not an original-language grapheme invariant.

items.finding: Both distinguish quoted declaration from institutional success and classify ineffectiveness/authority as defeasible. A explicitly leaves corridor as speech location versus origin open; B phrases it as speech location.
items.disposition: Do not assert a formal invalidity or successful closure. Preserve the corridor relation without resolving the attachment more narrowly than needed.

items.finding: Both recognize quoted mutual-understanding content and concurrent tongue-prosthesis action. A C04 marks inferred wordplay required=false; B C03 marks inferred wordplay required=true. A's policy still says retain lexical interaction where possible.
items.disposition: Keep the required-flag disagreement open. Separate source assertion, availability of a reading, and required preservation of that reading. Clarify the scope of required before a new blind run; do not overwrite either answer.

items.finding: Both require refusal, focused identification of Peter and others' agreement. Agreement does not entail completed signatures; focus is more specific than scalar salience.
items.disposition: Encode identity focus and contrast explicitly; preserve the relevant-group restriction.

items.finding: Both retain separate reports, Boris's stronger speech stance and narrator uncertainty. A lists competing reports as an optional inference; B discusses rivalry in alternatives. Neither chooses truth or adds lying/exclusive possession.
items.disposition: Retain competing attribution and suspension of judgment. Missing separate commitment row is not rejection of rivalry.

items.finding: Both require the hedge and already within the qualified proposition, without numeric confidence, precise evidence, or a missed journey.
items.disposition: Do not represent departure time as certain merely because temporal content was extracted separately.

items.finding: Both preserve empty envelope, Lena's conclusion, evening noticing and letter-on-box-lid location. Both keep possible reconsideration optional and preserve order in policy. B also mentions a possible cause of Lena's conclusion; A does not separately mention that causal link.
items.disposition: Do not add causal or belief-revision assertions, or merge envelope and box. Treat the extra optional inference as coverage, not conflicting required content.
